approach: Invert the one idiom that caused the defect: the eight editing callbacks on the key-grid surfaces become REQUIRED props, so an unmountable affordance fails tsc instead of rendering inert. On top of that, reach Developer parity in five sequential slices matching the spec's user stories: layer selector, KeymanWeb last-key stretch plus a per-row metrics readout replacing the withdrawn slack hatch, one merged property panel with all eight editable fields plus delete and four self-hiding move buttons, gesture editing in key mode, and unrequested id/keycap proposals. Engine additions stay narrow -- four fields admitted to EditableKeyFields, a move operation, two diagnostic codes, two proposal modules -- and no Pattern/Criterion type is touched.

decisions.decision: Make every editing callback on KeyGrid/KeyGridCell/the property panel a REQUIRED prop, deleting the optional-chaining call sites and undefined render guards.
decisions.why: The root cause is one idiom: eight optional on* props with exactly one caller turned eight compile-time errors into eight silent runtime nothings, and the three components disagreed about absence (cell hides, grid renders a dead button, inspector renders a reverting radio). Required props move the whole defect class to tsc, which runs in the PR lane.
decisions.rejected: An ESLint rule requiring the props at the call site (a weaker second statement of what the type system says once, and blind to props added later); a dev-mode runtime warning (the failure is already silent at runtime); a single commands object prop (larger refactor for the same guarantee, and it hides which handlers a mount supplies).

decisions.decision: Satisfy FR-009 (PR-lane coverage) with a vitest integration test mounting the real TouchGallery in key mode; un-skip the Playwright walk for FR-008 but do not treat it as the PR-lane guarantee.
decisions.why: ci.yml runs typecheck, pnpm -r test, lint and three standalone vitest configs -- and no Playwright step, so E2E genuinely runs outside the PR lane, exactly as the spec says. TouchGallery.test.tsx already mounts the real component with real store state across 5756 lines, so the harness exists.
decisions.rejected: Adding a Playwright job to ci.yml -- a CI-infrastructure change (browser downloads, runtime budget, flake policy) with a separate owner and scope, and FR-009 is satisfiable today without it.

decisions.decision: Merge KeyInspector and AssignPanel into one KeyPropertyPanel at US3; the proposal machinery is reached from the id field behind a disclosure.
decisions.why: The current mount stacks a read-only inspector above an editing panel, so complaint #2 (no fields editable) is partly an artifact of the DISPLAY panel being the one that looks like the property panel. Developer presents one panel. Keeping AssignPanel onCommit inherits the Case A/Case B promotedLayout split the e2e header warns an add/remove commit must not skip.
decisions.rejected: Keep both and make KeyInspector editable (two panels editing one key is worse than the split); add the missing fields to KeyInspector only (the author would edit sp in one panel and output in another).

decisions.decision: Add MoveKeyOp as a direction delta {left|right|up|down} carrying no key spec, and admit hint/width/pad/layer to EditableKeyFields.
decisions.why: move cannot be composed from remove+add: NewKeySpec carries no sk/multitap/flick/nodeId/provenance, so a re-add discards every sub-key and mints a fresh nodeId -- the identity key addressing, the decision trail and spec 035 Case B byte-preservation all key off. A delta lets both appliers splice the existing node, making FR-021 a property of the strategy rather than of a field-copy list that goes stale. All four fields already exist on TouchKeyIR; EditableKeyFields has no zod mirror, so Article I is not engaged.
decisions.rejected: An absolute {toRow, toIndex} target (stale under replay, since an earlier op may have changed the row length, whereas a direction re-resolves against current state); admitting a row-level width op so Even out row could work (already rejected by ADR 0002 and withdrawn by FR-007).

decisions.decision: Edit-time crowding reads Layer C check-18-3 thresholds from one shared exported table rather than restating them; the new finding is TOUCH_KEY_ROW_CROWDED at scope layer, severity warning.
decisions.why: check-18-3 already owns MAX_KEYS {phone:10, tablet:13} with desktop unruled and counts via the canonical isSpacerKeyClass predicate -- which already makes the all-blank-row edge case correct. The spec Assumptions say thresholds come from the existing hygiene check. RemoveKeyDialog.tsx:235 already restates that table once, so this prevents a third copy.
decisions.rejected: Duplicate the literal in the engine diagnostic (a third copy of a two-row table); move the check itself into Layer A/B (it is hygiene by Article IV, and FR-014 asks for an edit-time report, not a re-layering).

decisions.decision: Confine compatibility decomposition (NFKD) to a new keycapRelatedness.ts, which owns both proposeKeycap and the five-test isKeycapRelated guard.
decisions.why: FR-036 needs NFKD to make a localized number row (1 vs Arabic-Indic one) count as related, which is what SC-008 measures -- but the house rule forbids compatibility decomposition for character IDENTITY. The spec Assumptions carve it out for the display heuristic only. Isolating it in one module whose docstring states the carve-out keeps the blast radius readable in a single file.
decisions.rejected: Fold relatedness into touchKeyDiagnostics.ts -- that file would become the one place NFKD leaks in, without a docstring boundary saying why.

decisions.decision: FR-029/FR-030 inherited-id logic lives in a new proposeTouchKeyId wrapper that tries inherit then existing-producer then delegates to proposeKeyId; KeyIdMintingPath gains an inherited member.
decisions.why: proposeKeyId implements the four minting rows and states in its own docstring that it never scans an IR -- the caller supplies the facts. FR-029 needs the TouchKeyRuleIndex to ask what the inherited id actually produces, so it belongs one level up in pattern-apply. FR-030 never by geometric proximity becomes structural rather than a promise: the request shape carries no row, index or coordinate, so the only askable question is producedByKeyId.
decisions.rejected: Extend proposeKeyId with a rule index -- it would make a pure, IR-free, heavily unit-tested function depend on an index for one of five callers.

decisions.decision: Split the two test tools by role: Playwright is the EXPLORATION tool (drive the real SPA from the CLI, ad hoc, headed/--debug, to discover whether a surface behaves); vitest carries every DURABLE assertion in the PR lane. FR-008 un-skip is still delivered and must pass unmodified, but its standing is evidence, not a gate.
decisions.why: ci.yml has no Playwright step, so a Playwright-only assertion is not a regression guard -- it is a thing someone once observed. The split is lossless because TouchGallery.test.tsx already mounts the real component against real store state AND reaches the emitted artifact via runTransform(id), which returns the VFS map, so emitted-.keyman-touch-layout assertions need no browser.
decisions.rejected: Adding a Playwright job to ci.yml (a CI-infrastructure change with a separate owner and scope); leaving SC-005 to the e2e walk alone (it would rest the feature strongest safety claim entirely on the lane that does not run).

decisions.decision: Give SC-005 (untouched files byte-identical, untouched keys structurally identical) a vitest twin alongside the e2e walk copy.
decisions.why: Under the Playwright-explores/vitest-gates split, SC-005 assertions living only in the skipped e2e walk would leave the feature strongest safety claim ungated. No browser is needed: apply edits through the mounted component, call runTransform, and compare the emitted VFS against the shipped source. Two independent statements of a fidelity claim is proportionate for the one criterion about not corrupting the author keyboard.
decisions.rejected: One copy only -- either in vitest (losing the full-walk realism the e2e provides) or in Playwright alone (ungated).

decisions.decision: Fix the Case B IR-round-trip defect inside spec 065, in its own commit (out-of-scope-but-unblocking, per the cadence rule)
decisions.why: SC-006 assertion (c) is correctly catching a real spec-035 R9 violation; amending the assertion would mask a defect that destroys the touch provenance model after a single edit
decisions.rejected: Normalizing (c) to ignore the p stamp and filing the defect separately; or leaving (c) failing with FR-008 unmet

decisions.decision: Split Enter and F2 at the grid: Enter opens the key-property-panel region (FR-020b unchanged), F2 lands directly in the character field, opening the assign disclosure on the way
decisions.why: Restores spec 063 SC-004 keyboard-only assign inside its 12-action budget without reopening the property-panel remodel or weakening FR-020b; F2-edits-the-value is the grid convention and the key was already claimed
decisions.rejected: Amending SC-004 budget; or opening the assign disclosure by default (partly reopens research D3)

tasks.summary: 62 tasks across 8 phases: Setup (1) + Foundational required-prop inversion (7, blocks everything) + one phase per user story US1-US5 (8/11/12/4/11) + Polish (8). Waves are explicit with join lines; all 40 FRs mapped.
tasks.key_finding: US3 must follow US2, not just US1: FR-015 (declared width is a minimum) is a statement about the property panel width field that is only TRUE once the last-key stretch renders, so building the panel first would ship a width field whose help text was wrong. Every TouchGallery.tsx task is deliberately serialized -- 6,147 lines, all wiring lands there.

FR-001.title: Every editing callback on a key-mode surface MUST be a required input, not optional; a surface that cannot act MUST fail to build rather than render inert.

FR-002.title: The studio MUST supply handlers for all key-mode editing affordances: key type, apply-fix, add-key, remove, rename, and follow-next-layer.

FR-003.title: No key-mode control may render in a state where activating it has no effect; an affordance that does not apply MUST be absent.

FR-004.title: Key mode MUST provide a layer selector covering every layer of the active platform, including layers no key's next-layer reaches.

FR-005.title: The layer selector MUST group layers by family and plane, and MUST show each layer's rolled-up diagnostic count without the author visiting it.

FR-006.title: Following a key's next-layer MUST switch the selector to that layer.

FR-007.title: The Fill row and Even out row controls MUST be removed.

FR-008.title: The add/remove end-to-end walk MUST be un-skipped and MUST pass unmodified.

FR-009.title: Key-mode editing MUST be covered by a test that runs in the lane a pull request runs.

FR-010.title: The grid MUST render the touch layer's own geometry and MUST NOT derive sizing from the desktop layout.

FR-011.title: Row scale MUST be proportional to the layer maximum - the largest row total in the layer.

FR-012.title: The last key in every row MUST render stretched to the layer maximum; the slack hatch MUST be removed.

FR-013.title: Each row MUST report its interactive key count, total key width, total padding, and row total.

FR-014.title: A row exceeding the platform's key maximum MUST be reported as a non-blocking warning on that row, at edit time; exceeding it MUST NOT be prevented.

FR-015.title: A key's declared width MUST be presented as a minimum, distinct from its rendered width, with the distinction stated to the author.

FR-016.title: A newly added key MUST take the standard default width; the editor MUST NOT split an anchor key's width and MUST NOT normalize the row.

FR-017.title: Adding a key MUST NOT clip content, produce a negative width, or make any row unrenderable.

FR-018.title: Selecting a key MUST open one panel exposing keycap, hint, id, key type, modifier override, next layer, width and padding - all editable.

FR-019.title: The panel MUST offer delete, presenting the three outcomes (reflow, redistribute, suppress) with a proposal derived from the layer's kind.

FR-020.title: The panel MUST offer move left, right, up and down; each MUST be absent when it cannot act, and moves MUST NOT wrap across row boundaries.

FR-021.title: Moving a key MUST preserve its identity, sub-keys, geometry and provenance.

FR-022.title: The + between keys and at both row ends MUST be the only editing affordance on the grid itself.

FR-023.title: Every keycap MUST display its key id.

FR-024.title: Key mode MUST use the full pane width and MUST NOT render the live OSK preview; character mode MUST continue to render it.

FR-025.title: Switching between character mode and key mode MUST remain lossless in both directions.

FR-026.title: Key mode MUST allow adding, editing and removing longpress alternates, multitap entries, and all eight flick directions on the selected key.

FR-027.title: A selected sub-key MUST expose its gesture type, keycap and text for editing.

FR-028.title: Sub-key edits made in either mode MUST be visible in the other.

FR-029.title: When a touch key's inherited physical id still produces the intended default and modifier outputs, the editor MUST propose keeping it and MUST write no rule.

FR-030.title: For a newly added key, the editor MUST propose an id by asking whether any physical key already produces the character - never by geometric proximity.

FR-031.title: Where neither applies, the existing minting policy stands: a Unicode id by default; a custom id only for combining marks, multi-codepoint strings, and case triples.

FR-032.title: Every character class an author can reach MUST have a proposal path; where none is possible the editor MUST state why.

FR-033.title: Assigning a character MUST propose a keycap - a dotted-circle carrier for a combining mark, the character itself otherwise.

FR-034.title: A standalone (uncarried) keycap MUST be offered as an explicit non-default alternative, with its rendering consequence stated.

FR-035.title: Once the author edits a keycap by hand, later output changes MUST NOT rewrite it.

FR-036.title: A keycap/output mismatch MUST be reported only on character-class keys, only when unrelated by every relatedness test, at hint severity, never blocking.

FR-037.title: All author-facing copy MUST be studio-composed and localized; the engine MUST return structured fields, never English prose.

FR-038.title: The grid MUST remain a conformant ARIA grid, keyboard-operable throughout; the spec 063 SC-009 row-actions accessibility fix MUST NOT regress.

FR-039.title: New diagnostics MUST ride the existing single validation debounce cycle; no second timer may be introduced.

FR-040.title: Every edit MUST remain undoable, and the undo affordance MUST continue to name what it will undo.

concerns.note: PRE-EXISTING spec-063 defect surfaced by un-skipping the SC-006 walk (blame: ef19aa2b, not spec 065). TouchGallery.tsx:2527 - for Case B (imported/import-adapt) every key edit does store.setTouchLayoutJson(emitTouchLayout(promotedLayout)), a full IR round-trip. Measured effect: all 112 keys gain p=hand-set and sp/width/pad normalize to strings. This contradicts spec 035 R9, which applyKeyEditsToRawJson + projection step 1.7 (applyKeyEditsToVfs) exist to honour. Consequence: after one touch key edit an imported layout is entirely hand-set, so re-propagation can never update any key, and per-key layer/default plus platform displayUnderlying/fontsize that the IR does not model are dropped. Blocks SC-006 assertion (c). Complication for any fix: layoutForLintAndGate parses touchLayoutJson for the live grid, so the write cannot simply be deleted; and step 1.7 already re-applies the same overlay, so a naive Case B applier swap risks double-apply.

SC-004 REGRESSION, needs a decision (same class as the T016 one). Spec 063 SC-004 measures a keyboard-only assign in <=12 actions with Enter from the grid landing straight in AssignPanel character field. Spec 065 T028-T039 made Enter focus the key-property-panel REGION instead (correct per the new FR-020b, and asserted by touch-key-grid-a11y), and put the assign surface behind a disclosure inside it. So the author now needs Enter + tab-to-disclosure + Enter + tab-to-field, which likely blows the 12-action budget. This is a design consequence, not a stale test premise: either the panel needs a keyboard shortcut back to the character field, or SC-004 is amended. e2e touch-key-assign fails at the Enter step until decided. Separately: focusAssignPanelCharacterField was silently dead (querySelector for an input the closed disclosure keeps out of the DOM) - repaired to open the disclosure first, which fixes the fix-driven assign path, but that repair is not covered by a test.
